text: Hi guys! If you don’t know how to get texture packs in minecraft education, follow these steps. But first if you guys have issues PLEASE kindly reply to me. First go to 9Minecraft in google or safari {this works for all devices that use minecraft education} then search the kind of texture pack you wanna use. It can be anything you want. Click on your texture pack you chose, then press mcpack Meaning minecraft pack. Then press the button a couple of times until it says 9minecraft. Then, click on the button. After that when the pack gets downloaded, click on the download button OR your files. Press on the downloaded file. Make sure it isn’t a zip. Click on the file and then, magic! It takes you to minecraft education edition! Then, you’ll find something that says: “Succesfully imported your texture pack” if you don’t know how to open your texture pack, click settings. Go to resource packs in settings and go to my packs. Click on your texture pack and activate it. Choose the world you want to add the texture pack in. Then click the world, press settings and go to resource packs. Press my packs activate the texture pack, press play and you’ll see your pack RIGHT AWAY! I really hope you enjoy the texture pack you activated. You can also deactivate your pack by clicking on settings, going to resource packs and then press active. Then click on the texture pack you wanna deactivate. This is not supported by minecraft eduaction.

title: Some issues
text: MOJANG PLEASE READ THIS The game is basically a no cost version of Minecraft. But there are quite a lot of issues. Firstly, after a recent statewide data breach (Victoria, Australia) my password was reset by my school, thus I was signed out, I went to the demo page and all there was were simply boring adventure mode mini games that kind of teach nothing. I understand the application is for Educational Purposes Only, but it would be fun to be able to play without an account, I do understand that it makes the game "less safe", and I understand that Mojang chose safe over fun, which upsets quite of the users. Secondly, I created a Minecraft skin (custom) and found a guide, the guide said that through an "Owned" button in the UI I could change my skin. But turns out my school blocked changing any skin at all, what's the whole point of creating something that just gets blocked by ninety-five percent of schools, it's like Pythag, no one needs to know that the hypotenuse of a right angle triangle is the squares of the other sides added together, there is no point. Thirdly, a very common complaint is the updates, I understand that Mojang has said that Education Edition is being updated this month (January 2026), but can you at least update it earlier at the time Bedrock is updated. In conclusion, I would think that only limited changes to the game would be extremely controversial. Now I have programmed before and I understand that such changes could take like forever, but I hope that these changes can be implemented and soon though. Kind regards, Joshua Vella

title: very long to download🤬
text: Minecraft Education is often praised for helping students learn through games, but many students and teachers find it frustrating because it is difficult to download and takes too much time to set up. While the game itself can be educational and creative, the long installation process and technical problems can make users lose interest before they even start playing. These issues can make Minecraft Education Edition feel more stressful than enjoyable. One major problem with Minecraft Education Edition is that downloading the game can be confusing. Unlike regular Minecraft, users usually need a school account or special login information. Many students do not know their passwords or cannot access the correct account. Sometimes schools block downloads on student devices, meaning students must ask teachers or technology staff for help. This slows everything down and wastes valuable class time. Another issue is that the game file can take a long time to install. On slow computers or weak internet connections, the download may take several minutes or even hours. In schools where many students are downloading the game at once, the internet may become overloaded. This can cause the installation to freeze, fail, or restart completely. Students may become impatient and distracted while waiting for the game to work. Updates are another reason why Minecraft Education Edition can be annoying. The game often requires updates before users can play. These updates can be large and time-consuming, especially on older devices. Some students may finally open the game only to discover that another update is needed. This repeated waiting can ruin excitement and waste learning time during lessons. Technical problems also make the experience worse. Sometimes the game crashes, login screens do not work, or worlds fail to load properly. Younger students may not know how to solve these issues, forcing teachers to spend extra time troubleshooting instead of teaching. In some cases, students may never get the game running correctly at all. The complicated setup process can also make Minecraft Education Edition less accessible. Not every student has a modern computer or fast Wi-Fi at home. Students with older devices may struggle to download or run the game smoothly. This creates unfair situations where some students can participate easily while others fall behind because of technical limitations. In conclusion, Minecraft Education Edition has good educational ideas, but the difficult download process and long setup times can create frustration for both students and teachers. Slow installations, constant updates, login problems, and technical issues can waste time and reduce enjoyment. If the game were easier and faster to access, more students would likely have a better learning experience.
